clue.text: Group finds corpse

definitions.meaning: a ... is an organised group of people, as in a governing ...
a dead person's remains, as found by a detective

explanation.surface: A team stumbles on a dead person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an assembly of people acting as one, and the remains of someone dead.

clue.text: Poor prospect for inefficient guard

definitions.meaning: a sentry who keeps watch poorly, read literally

explanation.surface: A careless sentry offers a gloomy outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for a gloomy outlook is read literally as a sentry who does the job badly.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a gloomy future, and literally a watchman who is no good at watching.

clue.text: Pottery expert crushing novice

indicators.note: the skilled word squeezes the learner between its letters, holding it within

parts.note: deft means skilful, expert
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A skilled potter flattens an apprentice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushing' puts L inside DEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue-and-white glazed earthenware named after the Dutch town where it was made.

clue.text: Seaweed? Stop! Snake is hiding inside

indicators.note: the snake word is concealed within the word for stop, tucked between its letters

parts.note: to block is to stop or obstruct
an adder is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A warning cry about a snake lurking in seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop!' reads as a shouted warning, but it is a plain synonym; 'hiding inside' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Badderlock is an edible brown kelp of North Atlantic coasts, also called dabberlocks.

clue.text: A time spent getting dressed

parts.note: spent means exhausted, worn out

explanation.surface: Getting ready to go out takes a long while.
explanation.definitionFit: Attired is clothed, decked out in garments.

clue.text: Odd assortment of jewels but fair source of revenue

indicators.note: an assortment is a mixed collection, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: gems are jewels

explanation.surface: A strange mix of precious stones nonetheless earns money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assortment of' rearranges ODD to DOD. The fair is a funfair, where bumper cars take money from riders.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgems are bumper cars, a ride at a travelling funfair that brings in takings.

clue.text: Roof worker sent up in flames again

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending a word up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tiler lays tiles on roofs

explanation.surface: A roofer is blown upward by a fresh blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns TILER round.
explanation.definitionFit: Relit means set alight once more, ignited a second time.

clue.text: Duel with Rover may be officially disallowed

indicators.note: suggests the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A fight with a dog named Rover could be banned by the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges DUEL and ROVER together.
explanation.definitionFit: Overruled describes a decision set aside by someone with higher authority, such as a judge or referee.

clue.text: Cross? But this is a sign of affection

definitions.meaning: a cross, the letter X, written at the end of a letter stands for this
a touch of the lips given to show love

explanation.surface: An angry person is asked whether this shows fondness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry', but it is the X written at the foot of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The X at a letter's end stands for this caress, which is itself a token of love.

clue.text: Incredulous person confusing gain with cost

indicators.note: confusing letters mixes them up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sceptical mixes up profit and expense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusing' rearranges GAIN and COST together.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic doubts that God's existence can be known, so is a disbeliever of sorts.

clue.text: Very pleased to see the lamp in action

definitions.text: Very pleased to see the lamp in action

parts.words: Very pleased to see the lamp in action
parts.note: reads as overjoyed, while hinting at a lamp that has been switched on, lit up

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled to watch a lamp working.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half plays on the word's tail: a lamp in action has been lighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Delighted means greatly pleased, and its ending is the participle for set alight.

clue.text: Foreigners losing all initial rights

indicators.note: the word for foreigners drops a letter, losing it

parts.note: aliens are foreigners, people from another country

indicators.note: the first letter of the word all is the one dropped

explanation.surface: Immigrants are stripped of all their basic entitlements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' and 'initial' take A, the first letter of 'all', from ALIENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Liens are legal claims to hold property until a debt is paid, a kind of entitlement.

clue.text: Best alfresco party

parts.note: alfresco means outdoors, out in the open air
a do is a party, a social event

explanation.surface: The finest kind of party is held outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat them, surpass them.

clue.text: Resumes logging?

parts.note: read as going back in to record things in a log, or getting back into a system

explanation.surface: Someone goes back to cutting timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'logging' suggests felling trees, but it is making entries in a log, which is done over again.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enter is to go back in, or to record an item once more.

clue.text: Manufacture has importance — to supply a deficiency

definitions.note: the definition describes the thing's purpose rather than naming it as a noun

parts.note: to make is to manufacture
weight means importance, as in carrying weight

explanation.surface: Production matters when making up a shortfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeweight is something added to bring a quantity up to the required amount.

clue.text: Made a jumper's bones come together

definitions.meaning: produced a woollen pullover with needles and yarn
broken bones heal and join up

explanation.surface: A sweater was made, and a broken bone healed.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater; broken bones are also said to do this as they mend.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both working yarn into a sweater and fractured bones fusing as they heal.

clue.text: Umpire choked by dill pickle? Questionable diagnosis!

indicators.note: the umpire word is held inside, gripped round the throat by the other letters
a pickle is a muddle, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: a judge is an umpire, one who rules on a contest

explanation.surface: A referee chokes on a gherkin, and the doctor's verdict is doubtful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' makes ILLD from the dill, and 'choked by' signals the container. 'diagnosis' is surface colour, a doctor's verdict that is doubtful.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-judged means unwise, showing poor judgement, hence open to question.

clue.text: Naughty ladies I put in seats meant for clergy

indicators.note: naughty means badly behaved, so these letters misbehave into a new order

explanation.surface: Badly behaved women are seated in the clergy's stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' rearranges LADIES and I together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedilia are stone seats, usually three, set in a church chancel wall for priests.

clue.text: Holding device, I set out to enter harbour

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go into the harbour word, entering it

parts.note: a dock is a harbour basin for ships

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone heads for port with a gripping tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes IEST from 'I set', and 'to enter' signals the container. A diestock is an engineer's tool, not a farm word.
explanation.definitionFit: A diestock is a tool holding the dies used to cut screw threads.

clue.text: Releases hair from bun, apart from first bit

indicators.note: the word bun is used without its opening letter

parts.note: locks are hair, tresses

explanation.surface: Someone lets their hair down from a bun, except a little bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart from first bit' takes B off BUN, leaving UN.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlock is to unfasten or set free.

clue.text: Rumbles in it — or snores, maybe?

definitions.text: Rumbles in it — or snores, maybe?

indicators.note: a query on how the letters could be arranged, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A tummy rumbling or heavy snoring happens during sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges RUMBLES, and the whole clue describes deep sleep, during which a sleeper may rumble or snore.
explanation.definitionFit: Slumber is sleep, the state in which one might rumble or snore.

clue.text: Time to change ends, and not before time!

definitions.text: Time to change ends, and not before time!

parts.words: Time to change ends, and not before time!
parts.note: in cricket, bowling switches ends after each set of six balls; this is late in coming

explanation.surface: A player says a switch of ends has come too late.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowling changes ends after each over, so the first part is OVER; 'not before time' gives the sense of long-awaited.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue means late, past the time when it was expected.

clue.text: Nothing at breakfast? You should have porridge

parts.note: O is the number zero, nothing
breakfast is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone skips breakfast and is told to eat porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is ground oats, and in American usage the hot cereal cooked from them.

clue.text: Parachutist's gear?

parts.note: playfully, kit for someone who leaps from planes

explanation.surface: Asking what a skydiver wears.
explanation.walkthrough: A one-piece overall, named as if for someone who leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumpsuit is a one-piece garment, originally worn by skydivers.

clue.text: It helps the climber no end; going up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: no tip, a tip being the end of something

explanation.surface: A climber's aid gives endless help on the ascent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns NO TIP round.
explanation.definitionFit: A piton is a metal spike hammered into rock to secure a climbing rope.

clue.text: Trouble starts with port — it gives you wind

indicators.note: the start of the word trouble is taken

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Drinking port causes trouble by giving you flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' looks like the gas, but it is the verb, to coil.
explanation.definitionFit: To twine is to twist or coil around something.

clue.text: Hibernian flag over hospital

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sits over, above, the next

parts.note: a flag is a type of iris, the yellow flag

explanation.surface: An Irish flag flies above a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland. 'flag' is not a banner but the wild iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernian means of Ireland, from Hibernia, the Roman name for that island.

clue.text: Hence an attempt to succeed the Queen

indicators.note: to succeed is to come after, so the attempt follows the Queen

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a go is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: Therefore someone tries to take over from the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to succeed' looks like 'to win' but means 'to follow'; ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, so it means consequently.

clue.text: Correct title

definitions.meaning: a legal claim or entitlement, as in title to a property

explanation.surface: A heading has been approved.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: true or accurate, and a lawful claim or entitlement.

clue.text: Breakers are, when coming ashore, bearing right

definitions.note: the definition includes the verb, so the answer completes the phrase as a participle

indicators.note: the outer word carries, bears, the extra letter inside

parts.note: beaching is coming ashore

explanation.surface: Waves crash on the shore, moving to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' puts R inside BEACHING, after its first letter. Breakers here are waves, which break through a defence or barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaching means breaking through, which waves do to a sea wall.

clue.text: Gold coin I left at end of journey, following the custom

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
a dinar is a coin used in several countries

indicators.note: the last letter of journey is taken

explanation.surface: A traveller spends a final gold coin at the journey's end, as is usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinarily means usually, as a matter of normal practice.

clue.text: Pert young lady giving us the bill-to pay

definitions.meaning: a note of money owed, an invoice

explanation.surface: A saucy girl hands over the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a cheeky girl, and also a short note recording a sum owed.
